chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who dies and has a mother who is a slave, and has wealth, that his mother should be bought from his wealth and the remainder of the wealth be handed over to her, if there is no relative of hers who has a share in the Book (Quran).

key_terms.سَهْمٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ: Share in the Book (Quranic fixed share)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a deceased slave distributed if he leaves behind a slave mother?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the priority of freeing a slave mother from the deceased's estate before distribution to other heirs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on manumission as a means of spiritual and social elevation. The condition that no other relatives with fixed Quranic shares (such as parents or spouses) exist ensures that the estate is not fragmented, preserving the integrity of the inheritance system while prioritizing the mother's freedom. This specific legal precedent highlights the practical application of Quranic principles within the broader framework of Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the man who died and for him was a mother who was a slave, and for him was wealth that his mother should be bought from his wealth and the remainder be handed over to her when there do not happen to be any (other) relatives who have a (legislated) share in the Book (Quran)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this about the judgment of ’

Amir al-Mu’minin. It is about the case of a man who dies leaving behind a mother, who is owned by someone and a certain amount of assets. He (the Imam) has said, ‘His mother must be bought with his legacy and the rest of the legacy must be given to her, if there are no other relatives who have ordained shares according to the book.’”
